subject: Evaluating fitness (survival) values from Mark-Recapture modelling (Relative vs absolute)

messages.author: e9d15d3db318631b
messages.subject: Evaluating fitness (survival) values from Mark-Recapture modelling (Relative vs absolute)
parts:
I've been reading on the subject for a certain time and I can't wrap my head around the "type" of fitness we get out of a Mark-recapture hierarchical model with JAGS. 

In the article of Morrissey and Sakrejda (2013) UNIFICATION OF REGRESSION-BASED METHODS FOR THE ANALYSIS OF NATURAL SELECTION: 
http://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/evo.12077/abstract 

Two common analyses that are currently used to characterize selection are (1) least squares–based approximation of the individual relative fitness surface for the purpose of obtaining quantitatively useful selection gradients, and (2) spline-based estimation of (absolute) fitness functions to obtain flexible inference of the shape of functions by which fitness and phenotype are related. These two sets of methodologies are often implemented in parallel to provide complementary inferences of the form of natural selection.

I've used linear (quadratic) regressions to compute the survival probabilities and a spline to do the same thing with a capture history in JAGS. Is the first estimating relative survival and the second absolute? If yes, why?. 

Thanks,
